newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Sept 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Sept 15.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party leader Begum Khaleda Zia has warned her party will not remain silent if the government continues what she said "undemocratic behaviour and anti-people activities". Zia asked her party leaders and workers to be prepared for anti-government agitation.

India's Mizoram state had offered Bangladesh required volume of bamboo for paper and pulp production, said Salman F Rahman, chief of the Bangladesh Federation of Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FBCCI), on return from a business exploratory trip.

Loading and unloading at the Chittagong port came to halt on Saturday as dock workers began strike to press their demand for incentives. At least seven container vessels have been stranded at different jetties due to the strike.

Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, now visiting China, has urged Chinese entrepreneurs to invest in Bangladesh. She also asked for Chinese capital and expertise in infrastructure development in Bangladesh.
Bangladesh's commercial banks have accrued 98.35 bilion taka ($245 million) as classified loans -- bad, sub-standard and doubtful --, official sources said. -- Dhaka Newsroom 880-2-506363
